boring_rival_explanations: Small calibration set size per subject causes high-variance quantile estimates that happen to correlate with SRI by chance
General non-stationarity in physiological signals affects high-reactivity subjects more because their signals have larger dynamic range
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Undercoverage magnitude correlates with per-subject calibration sample count (n_calib) rather than SRI; when n_calib is matched across SRI tertiles, the SRI-undercoverage correlation disappears.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Stratify subjects by SRI tertile and downsample calibration sets to equal size per tertile. If SRI-undercoverage correlation persists (p<0.05, Spearman), H1 is supported; if correlation vanishes (p>0.2), the sampling-variability rival is supported.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: SRI must be computed from calibration-phase only. Control for fitness via IPAQ or estimated VO2max from resting HR. Medication inventory from WESAD health questionnaire. The rival exploits the fact that high-SRI subjects may have fewer usable calibration windows due to signal saturation.

possible_confounders: Skin type (Fitzpatrick scale) and hair density
control_variables: Ambient temperature (°C) and humidity (%) at recording
boring_rival_explanations: General PPG/EDA signal quality degradation (low SQI) reduces coverage uniformly across all subjects, not specifically those with high movement
Feature extraction pipeline fails on noisy segments regardless of movement source
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Stress-class coverage correlates with overall SQI (median across condition) but not with MAI specifically; subjects with low SQI from non-movement sources (e.g., poor perfusion) show equivalent undercoverage.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Regress stress coverage on MAI and SQI simultaneously. If MAI coefficient remains significant (p<0.05) after controlling for SQI, H2 is supported; if only SQI is significant (p<0.05) and MAI is not (p>0.2), the general-SQI rival is supported.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: MAI computed from ACC during TSST only. SQI uses Orphanidou 2015 template matching on BVP. Non-movement SQI degradation: simulate by adding Gaussian noise to clean PPG. Wrist circumference measured at sensor site. Strap tightness from post-session questionnaire.

possible_confounders: Cardiorespiratory fitness (faster recovery in fit individuals)
Hydration status (affects blood volume and HRV)
control_variables: Estimated VO2max (from resting HR and age)
Mean respiratory rate during recovery (breaths/min from RESP)
boring_rival_explanations: Any calibration set contamination (mislabeling, sensor drift, artifacts) inflates baseline conformity scores and narrows stress intervals, not specifically recovery-related contamination
Mondrian's class-conditional quantile estimation is biased downward for small calibration sets, affecting all subjects with few baseline samples
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Undercoverage correlates with any measure of baseline calibration contamination (e.g., proportion of baseline windows with stress-like features from any source), not specifically with recovery half-life exceeding ITI.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Compute baseline contamination from three sources: (1) slow recovery (H3), (2) simulated random mislabeling, (3) sensor drift. Regress stress coverage on each contamination measure. If only recovery-based contamination predicts coverage (p<0.05) while others do not (p>0.2), H3 is supported; if all contamination measures predict equally, the general-contamination rival is supported.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Recovery half-life: exponential fit to post-TSST RMSSD/EDA tonic. ITI = time from TSST end to next baseline-like condition (meditation). Contamination threshold: RMSSD < baseline_median - 0.5*(baseline_median - stress_median). Control for fitness via VO2max estimate. Respiratory rate from RESP belt to correct RMSSD.

possible_confounders: Education level and language proficiency (questionnaire comprehension)
Cognitive load during self-report (fatigue, time pressure)
Alexithymia (trait difficulty identifying feelings, distinct from interoception)
control_variables: Time since condition end to questionnaire (minutes)
Alexithymia score (TAS-20 if available, else proxy)
boring_rival_explanations: Random label noise at rate ~10-15% (typical for self-report) degrades conformal coverage uniformly, independent of interoceptive accuracy
Protocol labels are systematically biased (e.g., amusement condition rated as stressful by all subjects) causing stratum-wide miscalibration
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Injecting synthetic label noise at the observed discrepancy rate reduces coverage equally for all subjects; coverage does not correlate with individual label-physiology discrepancy after controlling for overall noise rate.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Simulate mislabeling: flip labels for windows where |self-report - PSI| > threshold. Measure coverage drop per subject. If coverage drop correlates with subject's actual discrepancy (p<0.05) beyond what synthetic noise predicts, H4 is supported; if synthetic noise alone explains coverage variance (R² > 0.8), the random-noise rival is supported.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: PSI = first PC of [EDA_phasic_rate, HR, -logRMSSD, RESP_rate] z-scored per subject. Discrepancy = |questionnaire_stress - PSI|. WESAD lacks direct IA measure; use discrepancy as proxy. Control for alexithymia via TAS-20 if available in extended metadata. Social desirability from post-study questionnaire.

possible_confounders: Prior TSST or public speaking experience
Time of day (cortisol rhythm affects stress reactivity)
boring_rival_explanations: General model misspecification (e.g., wrong nonconformity function) causes undercoverage for extreme feature values, not specifically due to stratification granularity
Any additional stratification variable (even random) improves coverage by reducing stratum size and quantile variance
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Re-stratifying by any continuous variable (e.g., random noise, baseline HR) improves stress coverage equally; WSI-based stratification provides no specific advantage over arbitrary stratification.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Compare coverage under three stratification schemes: (1) protocol label only (Mondrian), (2) WSI tertile + protocol label, (3) random continuous variable tertile + protocol label. If (2) improves coverage significantly more than (3) (paired t-test p<0.05), H5 is supported; if (2) and (3) improve equally (p>0.2), the arbitrary-stratification rival is supported.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: WSI = mean PSI during TSST. PSI as in H4. Trait anxiety = STAI-T (available in WESAD). Random variable: Gaussian noise matched to WSI variance. Stratification: create 3×3 = 9 strata (condition × tertile). Calibration: 70% per stratum per subject. Test: 30% held out.

possible_confounders: Sleep duration and quality previous night
Protocol order fatigue (later sessions more fatigued)
control_variables: Chronotype (MEQ score if available, else midpoint of sleep on free days)
Caffeine dose (mg) and time since last intake
boring_rival_explanations: Time-of-day effects are actually due to cumulative fatigue/protocol order: later recordings have more prior conditions, causing physiological drift
Morning/evening coverage difference reflects selection bias (different subject populations recruited at different times)
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Stress coverage correlates with session duration / number of prior conditions (fatigue) rather than clock time; when controlling for fatigue, recording time has no predictive power.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Regress stress coverage on recording time (continuous) and session duration (minutes from start to TSST) simultaneously. If recording time coefficient remains significant (p<0.05) after controlling for duration, H6 is supported; if only duration is significant (p<0.05) and time is not (p>0.2), the fatigue rival is supported.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: WESAD recording times from metadata (range ~09:00-17:00). Baseline sympathetic tone = mean EDA tonic (cvxEDA) + mean HR over 5-min pre-TSST baseline. Morning/evening split at median recording time. Chronotype: use MEQ if in extended data; else estimate from sleep midpoint. Fatigue proxy: session duration to TSST.

possible_confounders: Window length and overlap (60s/50% vs alternatives)
control_variables: Feature set (fixed 26 features: 12 EDA, 8 HRV, 6 RESP)
Preprocessing: bandpass filters, artifact rejection thresholds
Base classifier: fixed Random Forest (n_estimators=500, max_depth=10)
Interaction terms: fixed 3-way product of z-scored EDA_phasic, logRMSSD, RESP_rate
boring_rival_explanations: Curse of dimensionality: high-dimensional feature space causes sparse calibration coverage for all subjects, not specifically those with rare interaction profiles
Any dimensionality reduction (PCA, autoencoder) before conformity scoring improves coverage equally, not specifically interaction-aware methods
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Applying PCA to reduce to 3 dimensions before computing conformity scores improves coverage as much as interaction-aware stratification; the specific interaction structure is irrelevant.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Compare coverage under three conformity score constructions: (1) original 26 features, (2) PCA-3D features, (3) interaction-aware stratification (k-means on interaction features, k=4). If (3) outperforms (2) significantly (paired bootstrap p<0.05), H7 is supported; if (2) and (3) perform equally (p>0.2), the dimensionality-reduction rival is supported.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Interaction features: element-wise product of z-scored EDA_phasic_driver, logRMSSD, RESP_rate. Subject-wise logistic regression (stress vs baseline) with main effects + 3-way interaction. Weight = interaction coefficient. KL divergence via k-NN (k=5) on conformity scores. PCA on 26 features, keep 3 PCs. k-means on interaction features for stratification.

possible_confounders: Phenotype clustering method (k-means vs GMM vs hierarchical)
Features used for clustering (subject-level vs window-level)
Calibration set split randomness (70/30 split seed)
Base classifier randomness affecting conformity scores
control_variables: Clustering algorithm: Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) with BIC selection
Number of clusters: fixed k=4 (validated by silhouette)
Calibration split: fixed random seed (42) for reproducibility
Base classifier: fixed Random Forest seed (42)
boring_rival_explanations: Small total calibration size (~210 windows) causes high quantile variance for all subjects; rare phenotypes just happen to have fewer subjects by chance
Order statistic bias of empirical quantile affects all small strata equally, not specifically rare phenotypes
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Coverage correlates with per-subject calibration window count (n_calib_subject) regardless of phenotype; rare-phenotype subjects with matched n_calib show same coverage as common-phenotype subjects.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Match rare-phenotype and common-phenotype subjects on effective calibration size (subsample common-phenotype calibration windows). Compare coverage between matched groups. If rare-phenotype group still shows lower coverage (p<0.05, permutation test), H8 is supported; if coverage equalizes (p>0.2), the calibration-size rival is supported.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Phenotype features: [mean_PSI_TSST, EDA_phasic/HRV_ratio, HRV_recovery_slope]. GMM k=4. Effective size = sum of calibration windows from subjects in same cluster. Bootstrap quantile bias: resample calibration windows 1000x, compute 90th percentile, bias = mean(boot_q90) - pooled_q90. Matching: for each rare-phenotype subject, sample common-phenotype subject with closest effective size.

possible_confounders: Sensor age / battery level (affects EDA gain)
control_variables: Sensor serial number / age (months since manufacture)
Baseline skin hydration (corneometer if available, else baseline EDA tonic)
boring_rival_explanations: EDA baseline drift is caused by sensor aging/battery depletion over session duration, not temperature change
General EDA non-stationarity (slow tonic drift) occurs in all subjects and correlates with session time, not specifically with ΔT
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: EDA baseline shift (ΔEDA_tonic) correlates with sensor age / session duration rather than skin temperature change (ΔT); temperature normalization does not improve coverage beyond session-time detrending.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Regress ΔEDA_tonic on ΔT and session duration (minutes from baseline to TSST end) simultaneously. If ΔT coefficient remains significant (p<0.05) after controlling for duration, H9 is supported; if only duration is significant (p<0.05) and ΔT is not (p>0.2), the sensor-aging rival is supported. Additionally, apply temperature correction (k=0.07/°C) and session-time detrending; compare coverage improvement.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: ΔT = median(T_last_5min_TSST) - median(T_last_5min_baseline) from E4 thermistor. EDA tonic from cvxEDA. Phasic rate = SCR peaks/min (threshold 0.01 μS). Temperature correction: EDA_corrected = EDA_raw * exp(-0.07*(T - T_ref)). Session-time detrending: linear fit to EDA tonic over session, subtract trend. Sensor age from device logs if available.

possible_confounders: Baseline physical activity before recording (walking to lab)
control_variables: Protocol knowledge (self-report: 'did you know what TSST involves?')
GAD-7 score (if available, else STAI-T > 50 as proxy)
Pre-baseline activity (accelerometer counts in 30 min before baseline)
Caffeine dose (mg) and time since intake before baseline
boring_rival_explanations: Baseline contamination reflects incomplete physiological rest (subjects not fully relaxed) rather than anticipatory anxiety specifically
Mondrian's conformity score function (1 - softmax) inherently produces higher baseline scores for any subject with elevated baseline arousal, regardless of cause
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Baseline conformity score contamination correlates with pre-baseline physical activity (ACC magnitude) rather than STAI-T or AAI; subjects with high pre-baseline activity show contamination even with low STAI-T.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Regress baseline contamination rate on AAI and pre-baseline ACC magnitude (30-min window) simultaneously. If AAI coefficient remains significant (p<0.05) after controlling for ACC, H10 is supported; if only ACC is significant (p<0.05) and AAI is not (p>0.2), the incomplete-rest rival is supported. Verify rest: require ACC < 0.05g for 10 min pre-baseline.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: AAI = (mean_HR_baseline_last_5min - mean_HR_first_2min) / (mean_HR_TSST - mean_HR_first_2min). Baseline contamination: conformity score > median(stress_calibration_scores). Conformity score = 1 - softmax(stress_class) from base RF. Pre-baseline ACC: magnitude in 30 min before baseline start. STAI-T from WESAD. GAD-7 not in WESAD; use STAI-T > 50 as high-anxiety proxy. Experimenter ID from metadata.
